samples.summary: design-sandbox:check now declares a dependency on core's dist, but nothing selects that lane when core (or sheets) changes — its manifest names only design-editor
samples.evidence: The new comment/`needs` at scripts/verify-self.mjs:332-340 documents that design-sandbox's vitest resolves the ENGINES from src and `packages/sheets/src/view/theme.ts` pulls `@wafflebase/core/tokens` from core's built `dist/`. Lane selection, however, is derived from manifests: scripts/changed-areas.mjs:108-129 builds the graph purely from package.json `@wafflebase/*` deps, and packages/design-sandbox/package.json:15-19 declares only `@wafflebase/design-editor`. So `reverseClosure({core})` / `{sheets}` never contains `design-sandbox`, and harness.config.json marks the package inert so `pkgs` cannot reach it either — only the `designEditor` tag can. Net effect: a core- or sheets-only change never runs design-sandbox:check even though it can now break it (broken engine/token import, exactly the ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND the comment describes), and the failure lands on main. The `needs: ["core:build"]` edge only helps on runs where the lane was already selected. Fix belongs either in packages/design-sandbox/package.json (declare the engines/core it actually resolves) or in the lane's `pkgs`/tags.

samples.summary: New dry-run early returns are placed ahead of `parseOutputFormat`, so `--format` is no longer validated on those previews (unlike every sibling command)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25-37 returns the preview before `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` (which used to run first at cells.ts ~line 39); same shape at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:132 (`docs get`) and packages/cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:20 (`tabs list`). Every other dry-run site in this same diff validates first and says so (docs.ts:80-88 for `--type`, files.ts:87-99, sheets-export.ts:47-49), and packages/cli/test/api-keys.test.ts:6-11 encodes 'validate --format before anything else' as an existing contract, while docs/design/cli.md:1247 states `--dry-run` validates inputs. `sheets cells get doc-1 --format bogus --dry-run` now prints a preview instead of erroring.

samples.summary: `printDryRunUrl` drops the dot-segment invariant `printDryRun` enforces, so any caller that builds a URL some other way can print a walked-out preview
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:26) still calls `assertNoDotSegments(path)`, described at dry-run.ts:17-20 as 'the invariant it leaves behind'. The new sibling `printDryRunUrl` accepts a fully-built URL string and performs no check at all; today the only caller (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:44,61,81 via `apiKeysUrl`) is safe because `apiKeysUrl` runs `seg()`, but the exported entry point itself no longer carries the invariant that the existing `printDryRun` tests (packages/cli/test/dry-run.test.ts:144-156) were written to protect.

samples.summary: The new empty-segment refusal is CLI-only, and the browser client has call sites where an empty id does fall through to a collection route — contradicting url.ts's stated rationale
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:14-19 justifies keeping the empty-id refusal CLI-local with 'The browser client builds its URLs from ids it already holds, so it has no equivalent hole to close.' But packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:15 re-exports core `seg()` unchanged, and packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:49 (`GET ${BASE}/${seg(id)}` — `/workspaces/` is the list route) and packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:47 build the same trailing-slash shape from ids that flow in from route params/state. If any of those can be empty, the request silently addresses the collection for exactly the Express non-strict-routing reason given in the CLI comment. I could not confirm an empty id is reachable in the browser flows (would need to trace the `useParams`/store sources), hence low confidence.

samples.summary: `isLoopbackHost` returns true for a missing Host header, so any non-browser client can reach the callback handler without passing the new check
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:450 (`if (host === undefined) return true;`) is reached for any request that omits `Host` (HTTP/1.0 or a hand-rolled socket), so a local process — the threat model the surrounding comment at login.ts:479-503 names — still reaches the nonce check unchanged. The allowance is documented as deliberate ('a browser always sends one') and the nonce remains the real guard, so this is a note that the new guard's coverage is browser-only rather than a defect in the nonce path; deeper judgement on whether that is the right design belongs to the security lens.

verdict.reason: Verified all elements. verify-self.mjs:322-341 declares design-sandbox:check with pkgs ["design-sandbox"], tags ["designEditor"], needs ["core:build"], and the runtime dependency is real: vitest.config.ts:26 -> aliases.ts:61,68 alias sheets/docs/notes/slides/board to src; seed-sheets.ts:49 imports toSref from @wafflebase/sheets and is loaded by test/scenes/canvas/seeds.test.ts:3; packages/sheets/src/view/theme.ts:1 imports @wafflebase/core/tokens, which packages/core/package.json:18-23 resolves to dist/. Lane selection cannot reach that lane from a core/sheets change: changed-areas.mjs:108-129 builds the graph only from manifest @wafflebase/* deps, packages/design-sandbox/package.json:15-19 declares only @wafflebase/design-editor, and packages/design-editor/package.json:21-48 declares no @wafflebase dep, so reverseClosure(["core"]) (changed-areas.mjs:142-159) excludes design-sandbox; harness.config.json:40-49 marks packages/design-sandbox/** inert and classify short-circuits on inert (changed-areas.mjs:422-432), so laneSelected (changed-areas.mjs:580-585) can only fire via the designEditor tag. Existing guards do not cover it: changed-areas.test.mjs:834-866 only checks declared manifest edges into inert packages, and the needs closure (changed-areas.mjs:597-611) only applies once the lane is already selected; a push to main is unfiltered (changed-areas.mjs:546-550), so the breakage surfaces there. Real, reachable coverage gap in the blast-radius lane; nothing to refute it with.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding contains no code claim to verify. Its text is verbatim this repository's own runtime infra error: `scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637` (`poolExhaustedError`) produces "<label>: every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to", and `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1690-1695` (`lensFailureSummary`) wraps a lens's thrown error with the prefix "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: ". Together they mean the upstream blast-radius lens session never ran because the credential pool was drained — the panel then synthesises a placeholder major entry so the round pages a human (documented at scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2641 and consumed as INFRA at scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:565). The same event is already recorded for PR #873 in docs/tasks/active/20260820-fixer-live-credential-todo.md:9-11 ("the page came from the INFRA path, so no gate was ever consulted"). The finding names no file, line, symbol, changed contract, caller, guard, or bypassing site, so under the blast-radius rubric there is nothing present-as-described in the source: no broken caller, no removed export, no bypassed guard. Ground: not-present. Remediation is an infra re-run / credential registration (already tracked), not a source change. I saw no prompt-injection style steering in the files read.
